papers.title_en: CARVS: A Congestion-Aware Algorithm for Online Multi-Agent Pickup-and-Delivery in Human-Collaborative Warehouses
papers.authors: Chaoran Li, Zeyuan Zhao, Shao Zhang
papers.evidence: 仓库中的在线多智能体取送货路径规划
papers.tldr: 在人机协作仓库中，人类行为不确定会造成动态交互与机器人临时挡路，传统多智能体取送货（MAPD）难以及时响应。论文形式化MAPDwHC问题，并提出CARVS算法，将任务交换、验证检查与随机初始化融入任务分配和路径规划。仿真表明，CARVS在大规模场景显著减少路径规划超时，而传统MAPD易失败。该工作提升了拥堵环境下的人机协作适应性、实时性与可扩展性。
papers.abstract_en: Intelligent warehouse systems have transformed logistics by integrating robots with minimal infrastructure changes, boosting efficiency and optimizing workflows compared to traditional human-only operations. However, human-robot collaboration introduces new challenges, particularly due to human uncertainty, which leads to dynamic interactions and unpredictable behavior. To address these complexities, this paper presents the Multi-Agent Pickup-and-Delivery with Human Collaboration (MAPDwHC) problem, an extension of the Multi-Agent Pickup-and-Delivery (MAPD) problem that incorporates human unpredictability. This problem adds key constraints, such as dynamic obstacles caused by robots temporarily blocking paths when interacting with humans, and the need for real-time responsiveness. We formalize the MAPDwHC problem with additional constraints and properties. Based on this problem setting, we propose the CARVS algorithm, which improves task assignment and path planning by integrating task swapping, validation checks, and random initialization. CARVS reduces congestion, enhances adaptability to human-robot interactions, and ensures real-time responsiveness. Simulation results show that CARVS significantly reduces timeouts of path planning in large-scale scenarios where traditional MAPD algorithms fail, improving both efficiency and scalability.

papers.title_en: Policy Search in Code Space for Multi-Agent Pathfinding
papers.authors: Matthias Eder, Pantelis Emmanouil, Vivek Farias, Fabian Fischer, Adam Jozefiak, Tianyi Peng, Thomas Ulz, Raphael Watschinger, Fangyu Wu, Andrew Zheng
papers.evidence: 在多智能体路径规划中于代码空间搜索协调策略
papers.tldr: 多智能体路径规划长期依赖人工算法设计或不透明的强化学习。本文让编码智能体在代码空间迭代提出、实现、评估并修正策略，以仿真反馈和正确性验证驱动搜索。两案例中，该方法在机器人竞赛密集地图上超过复现强基线35.0%，并在模拟仓库中带来58.9%吞吐提升。研究表明代码空间策略搜索兼顾自动化、可解释与工程可验证性。
papers.abstract_en: Developing coordination policies for complex multi-agent systems relies on either labor-intensive algorithm design or opaque task-specific reinforcement learning. With recent advances in autonomous coding agents, we show that policy search directly in code space offers a compelling third path that combines automated optimization with explicit interpretability. We investigate a human-directed workflow in which coding agents iteratively propose, implement, evaluate, diagnose, and eventually refine algorithms guided by simulation feedback and explicit correctness verification. We conducted two case studies and found that this workflow robustly outperformed any manually engineered solutions. On a challenging map in the 2024 League of Robot Runners competition, a two-day search discovered a policy that exceeds the stronger locally reproduced competition entry by 35.0% on the densest instance and generalizes to unseen map instances. In simulated real-world warehouses with irregular lanes, continuous robot geometry, and asynchronous motion, a week-long search discovered an entirely new class of multi-agent pathfinding algorithm that outperforms a calibrated proprietary solution in throughput by 58.9%. Under stated assumptions, we further prove that the new algorithm is collision-free and completes, in finite time, every accepted goal that is not withdrawn or replaced. Together, the studies show that policy search in code space powered by state-of-the-art coding agents offers a highly competitive path to building real engineering solutions that are both effective and analytically tractable.

papers.evidence: 面向仓储物流的多智能体路径规划混合专家神经策略
papers.tldr: 针对多智能体路径规划中局部观测到动作分布的神经策略设计难题，本文从元层面引入混合专家（MoE）框架。方法先训练面向不同地图分布的紧凑专家，再学习路由器按智能体局部情境选择性融合专家输出，并以图神经网络策略和新递归动作令牌精炼模型实例化。实验表明MoE通常优于预训练策略并超过现有领先方法，但参数匹配且训练充分的单体模型仍更强。研究揭示了地图分布MoE在MAPF中的细微作用与适用边界。
papers.abstract_en: Designing capable neural policies for multi-agent pathfinding (MAPF), which map local observations to action distributions, represents an important challenge in multi-agent learning, with practical relevance to scalable collective automation problems such as warehouse logistics. In contrast to prior studies focusing primarily on individual policy design, this study explores a meta-level Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) approach to learning-based MAPF. Specifically, given a collection of compact yet high-performing experts specialised for different map distributions, our architecture learns a router that selectively fuses their outputs according to each agent's local situation. We instantiate and validate this MoE approach with a commonly used graph neural network-based policy as well as a newly developed recursive action-token refinement model. Combined with supervised and reinforcement learning fine-tuning of the experts, our experiments show that MoE generally improves upon the pretrained policy and outperforms existing leading methods. At the same time, our findings reveal that appropriately trained, parameter-matched monolithic models still outperform MoE, highlighting a nuanced role for map-distribution MoE for MAPF.

papers.title_en: CoopUQ: Robust Multi-Robot Social Navigation via Uncertainty-Aware Cooperative Forecasting
papers.authors: Zehao Wang, Jianpeng Yao, Yuping Wang, Yiping Li, Jiaqi Li, Zhixu Li, Kanghoon Lee, Jinfeng Wang, Cong Liu, Zhaowei Tan, Jinkyoo Park, Jiachen Li
papers.evidence: 基于不确定性感知协同预测的多机器人社交导航
papers.tldr: 多机器人共享人机环境中，把单机器人策略直接扩展到多机，在遮挡与分布外场景下难以保证安全与效率。CoopUQ 通过跨机器人时空特征融合预测未来占据栅格及其不确定性，并用约束多智能体强化学习，把预测为占据或高不确定的区域作为代价惩罚来引导策略。在多个 Unity3D 仿真（含分布外布局、人群密度与急促行为）及实机实验中，其预测性能与安全性均优于代表性基线，并展现跨场景鲁棒性。
papers.abstract_en: Reinforcement learning enables mobile robots to make fast and scalable navigation decisions in constrained human-shared environments. However, directly extending single-robot approaches to multi-robot settings often fails to ensure safety and efficiency, especially under occlusions and out-of-distribution (OOD) scenarios, where individual robots may overlook potential risks or make inaccurate predictions. Leveraging cooperation effectively for both prediction and navigation remains a major challenge. We propose CoopUQ, a multi-robot social navigation framework that bridges uncertainty-aware cooperative occupancy forecasting and robust decision making. CoopUQ predicts future occupancy grid maps through cross-robot spatiotemporal feature fusion and further leverages forecasts and their uncertainty to guide policy via constrained multi-agent reinforcement learning, where the cost penalizes navigation through regions predicted to be occupied or highly uncertain. This design enables the policy to adapt its risk sensitivity under distribution shifts. Experimental results across multiple Unity3D-based simulation environments with both in-distribution and OOD settings, including diverse layouts, pedestrian densities, and rushing behavior, demonstrate improved prediction performance and safety over representative baselines. Real-robot experiments further demonstrate its robustness across various scenes. Our code and videos are available at https://coopuq.github.io/.

papers.title_en: PACT: Plan-Augmented Coordination via Trace-Graphs for Dynamic Multi-Agent Combinatorial Optimization
papers.authors: Xiao Zhou, Alex Schutz, Victor-Alexandru Darvariu, Nick Hawes
papers.evidence: 面向动态路由与组合优化的多智能体协调
papers.tldr: 现实中的组合优化问题往往是动态的，相关信息随智能体行动逐步揭示，而现有方法假设实例信息已知，难以协调探索与利用。PACT在环境图上加入表示智能体计划的辅助节点，并与资源节点相连以指示未来依赖，通过增广图上的消息传递实现前瞻性冲突消解。实验表明PACT在动态问题上解质量优于基线，向更大实例迁移最佳，甚至超过可访问不确定性信息的中心化 oracle。
papers.abstract_en: Multi-agent approaches have been investigated recently as a means of improving the scalability of reinforcement learning for neural combinatorial optimization. Existing methods assume that all problem instance information is known upfront. However, real-world problems are often dynamic: relevant information is progressively revealed as the agents take actions (e.g., arriving at an edge in a routing problem only to discover it is untraversable). In such cases, existing methods fail to coordinate agents to explore and exploit the progressively revealed information. To address the arising coordination challenge, we introduce PACT (Plan-Augmented Coordination via Trace-graphs). PACT augments the environment graph with auxiliary nodes representing the plans of agents, which are connected to the resource nodes to indicate future dependencies. The proposed message-passing scheme over the augmented graph grounds inter-agent coordination in the environment and enables proactive, rather than reactive, conflict resolution. We show that PACT improves solution quality in dynamic problems relative to baselines and exhibits the best transfer to larger instances on which, remarkably, it outperforms centralized oracles with privileged access to instance uncertainty.
